headline: Council referred the 101 Elm Street car wash modification to committee and approved $120,000 for a cemetery truck.
summary: The council held hearings on a second-hand dealer's license at 1275 Main Street, a car wash at 101 Elm Street, and a special permit at 220 Moody Street. It referred several license and permit requests to committee. It also approved funds for a cemetery truck and grants for EV chargers and road safety, and it confirmed two Council on Aging members.
decisions: Referred the second-hand dealer's license for Hits and Hollows at 1275 Main Street to the licenses and franchises committee.
Referred the second-hand dealer's license for Roadshow Concepts LLC at 550 Winter Street to the licenses and franchise committee.
Recessed the public hearing on the special permit modification at 101 Elm Street until December 14th, 2026, and referred the matter to the Audiences and Rules Committee.
Recessed the public hearing on the special permit at 220 Moody Street until December 14th, 2026.
Placed on file the mayor's request for councilors to serve on a hockey rink design committee for the Lawrence School property, after councilors were recommended for the committee.
Referred to the finance committee the mayor's request to transfer $42,536 for the preliminary design phase of the repair of the firewall street bridge.
Referred to the finance committee the mayor's request for $56,760 to cover expanded work on the Chester Brook culvert at Beaver Street.
Referred to the finance committee the mayor's request for $40,000 for professional services.
Referred applications and licenses to the licenses and franchises committee.
Approved ten resolutions honoring firefighters who are retiring.
Confirmed Richard Pizzi Jr. as a permanent member of the Council on Aging, 12 in favor.
Confirmed Marsha McCleary as a permanent member of the Council on Aging, 12 in favor.
Approved a $120,000 appropriation from the cemetery sale of lots and graves account to buy a new pickup truck with a snowplow package for the cemetery division.
Approved accepting a $52,152 grant from the Office of Grants Research to support the FY 2027 municipal road safety program.
Approved accepting $9,000 in additional EECBG grant funds for installing new EV chargers in the city's public parking lots.
Approved on third and final reading the compensation ordinance for personnel costs tied to the election, 12 in favor.
Gave a first reading to a $462,755 loan order for additional design services for the fire administration wing of the police station, then placed it on the table.
Approved the fortune teller license at 24 Crescent Street for Manu Park.
Approved the extended hours renewal at 12 Harvard Street for CVS pharmacy number 114.

Approved the request that the mayor arrange for solar-powered trash and recycling compactors on the west side of Moody Street near the Riverwalk entrance, based on a McDevitt Middle School civics project.
Approved the 1725 petition at 205 Second Avenue for National Grid.
Approved the 1725 petition for South Street at Vernon Street for National Grid.
Granted leave to withdraw without prejudice the special permit application for 287 Crescent Street, 12 in favor.
discussion: Questions on the 101 Elm Street car wash modification covered traffic flow, keeping the site open during construction, the new pay stations, and sidewalk and water runoff problems. The attorney for the owner said the footprint, traffic flow, and existing conditions would stay the same, and councilors asked for more information in committee.
At 220 Moody Street, the applicant said it was still waiting for an appraisal of a potential easement and expected it within about a week.
A councilor reminded residents that early voting runs through this Friday and that election day is Tuesday, November 3. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Councilors honored ten retiring firefighters, and a retirement party was announced for October 29th.
